items.headline: U.S. Stocks Drift as Geopolitical Tensions and Rising Bond Yields Clash with AI Optimism
items.summary: U.S. equities showed a mixed performance in mid-day trading as investors navigated renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran, driving oil prices higher, and a continued sell-off in global bond markets, pushing Treasury yields to multi-year highs. This risk-averse sentiment was partially offset by persistent optimism surrounding artificial intelligence-related stocks and strong individual corporate earnings. The ADP National Employment Report indicated a slowdown in August job creation, while the ISM Manufacturing PMI showed continued, albeit slower, expansion in the manufacturing sector.

items.statContext: The S&P 500 inched up, showing a slight recovery amid broader market pressures.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced a marginal dip.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted a modest gain, indicating some resilience in blue-chip stocks.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Surges on Strong Earnings and AI Growth
items.summary: Dell Technologies surged nearly 10% in pre-market trading after reporting robust Q2 fiscal 2027 results, with revenue up 58% year-over-year and non-GAAP diluted EPS soaring 203%. The company's AI server business was a significant driver, contributing a 100% year-over-year increase in AI server revenue and leading to raised full-year guidance.

items.headline: GitLab Jumps in Pre-Market
items.summary: GitLab saw a significant leap of over 23% in pre-market trading, marking it as one of the strongest performers among tech stocks.

items.headline: Howmet Aerospace Declines on SpaceX In-House Manufacturing News
items.summary: Howmet Aerospace fell over 7% after Elon Musk's announcement that SpaceX plans to cast gas-turbine blades in-house, a move perceived as a threat to Howmet's specialized supply niche.

items.headline: Credo Technology Slips Despite Strong Earnings Beat
items.summary: Credo Technology weakened significantly in pre-market trading, falling more than 9% at one point, despite exceeding Q1 fiscal 2027 financial results and providing strong guidance.

items.headline: August Job Growth Slows, Manufacturing Expands at Slower Pace
items.summary: The ADP National Employment Report revealed that private companies added 38,000 jobs in August, a slowdown from 46,000 in July and below estimates, marking the slowest month since January. Concurrently, the ISM Manufacturing PMI for August eased to 54.6% from 55.6% in July, although it still signifies an eighth consecutive month of expansion for the sector.

items.headline: Fed Rate Hike Expectations Rise Ahead of September FOMC Meeting
items.summary: Following Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's recent hawkish remarks on inflation, expectations for a September Fed rate hike have risen to nearly 60%. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to meet on September 15-16, 2026, with the decision on the federal funds rate being a key focus for investors. Mortgage rates have already hit a one-year high.

items.headline: U.S.-Iran Hostilities Drive Oil Prices and Bond Yields Higher
items.summary: Renewed hostilities between the U.S. and Iran are intensifying concerns over global energy supplies, pushing crude oil prices higher, with Brent crude trading near $94.90 per barrel. This geopolitical tension, alongside elevated inflation, contributed to a deepening global bond market sell-off, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury note yield hitting a high of 4.814%, its highest level since November 2023.

items.headline: Broadcom, Snowflake, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Set to Report Earnings Today
items.summary: Several major companies are scheduled to report their earnings after the market close today, September 2. Among them are Broadcom ($AVGO), Snowflake ($SNOW), and Hewlett Packard Enterprise ($HPE). Broadcom's report is particularly anticipated, with investors keen on its AI chip revenue and fiscal 2027 AI guidance.
